messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 4-chloroanisole with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

Variables and options:
ligand:
L1: tBuBrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]
L2: tBuXPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C(C)(C)C)C(C)(C)C)C=CC=C2]
L3: XPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P(C3CCCCC3)C4CCCCC4)C=CC=C2]
L4: AdBrettPhos [SMILES CC(C)C(C=C(C(C)C)C=C1C(C)C)=C1C2=C(P([C@@]3(C[C@@H]4C5)C[C@H](C4)C[C@H]5C3)[C@]6(C7)C[C@@H](C[C@@H]7C8)C[C@@H]8C6)C(OC)=CC=C2OC]

base:
B1: BTMG [SMILES CC(C)(C)/N=C(N(C)C)/N(C)C]
B2: P2Et [SMILES CN(C)P(N(C)C)(N(C)C)=NP(N(C)C)(N(C)C)=NCC]
B3: MTBD [SMILES CN1CCCN2C1=NCCC2]

additive:
A1: 5-phenylisoxazole [SMILES C1(C2=CC=CC=C2)=CC=NO1]
A2: 4-phenylisoxazole [SMILES C1(C2=CC=CC=C2)=CON=C1]
A3: 3-phenylisoxazole [SMILES C1(C2=CC=CC=C2)=NOC=C1]
A4: 5-(dibenzylamino)isoxazole [SMILES C1(N(CC2=CC=CC=C2)CC3=CC=CC=C3)=CC=NO1]
A5: 3-(dibenzylamino)isoxazole [SMILES C1(N(CC2=CC=CC=C2)CC3=CC=CC=C3)=NOC=C1]
A6: 1,2-benzisoxazole [SMILES C12=C(C=CC=C2)ON=C1]
A7: 2,1-benzisoxazole [SMILES C12=CON=C1C=CC=C2]
A8: ethyl 5-methylisoxazole-4-carboxylate [SMILES CC1=C(C(OCC)=O)C=NO1]
A9: ethyl 5-methylisoxazole-3-carboxylate [SMILES CC1=CC(C(OCC)=O)=NO1]
A10: 3,5-dimethylisoxazole [SMILES CC1=CC(C)=NO1]
A11: 5-methyl-3-(pyrrol-1-yl)isoxazole [SMILES CC1=CC(N2C=CC=C2)=NO1]
A12: 5-methylisoxazole [SMILES CC1=CC=NO1]
A13: ethyl 3-methylisoxazole-5-carboxylate [SMILES CC1=NOC(C(OCC)=O)=C1]
A14: 3-methyl-5-phenylisoxazole [SMILES CC1=NOC(C2=CC=CC=C2)=C1]
A15: 3-methylisoxazole [SMILES CC1=NOC=C1]
A16: ethyl isoxazole-4-carboxylate [SMILES CCOC(C1=CON=C1)=O]
A17: ethyl isoxazole-3-carboxylate [SMILES CCOC(C1=NOC=C1)=O]
A18: ethyl 3-methoxyisoxazole-5-carboxylate [SMILES COC1=NOC(C(OCC)=O)=C1]
A19: 5-(2,6-difluorophenyl)isoxazole [SMILES FC(C=CC=C1F)=C1C2=CC=NO2]
A20: methyl isoxazole-5-carboxylate [SMILES O=C(OC)C1=CC=NO1]
A21: methyl 5-(furan-2-yl)isoxazole-3-carboxylate [SMILES O=C(OC)C1=NOC(C2=CC=CO2)=C1]
A22: methyl 5-(thiophen-2-yl)isoxazole-3-carboxylate [SMILES O=C(OC)C1=NOC(C2=CC=CS2)=C1]

Experiments so far (best first):
L3 | B1 | A11 -> 2.1%
L2 | B2 | A8 -> 1.9%

L3 | B3 | A16 -> 0.4%

Propose exactly 20 NEW experiments not listed above. Return JSON:
{"picks": [{"ligand": "<label>", "base": "<label>", "additive": "<label>", "reason": "<one sentence>"}]}

picks.reason: Tests whether the strong L3/B1/A11 result is robust to a different strong, non-nucleophilic base.
Completes the base comparison around the best observed L3/B1/A11 combination.
Isolates the ligand effect against the top additive and base while avoiding the previously poor L1/B2 pairing.
Tests whether MTBD improves the previously weak L1/A11 combination.
Evaluates tBuXPhos with the best observed base-additive pairing.
Compares MTBD with BTMG for tBuXPhos while holding the top additive fixed.
Tests the closely related AdBrettPhos scaffold under the most promising observed base-additive conditions.
Checks whether the bulky AdBrettPhos ligand benefits from the stronger phosphazene base.
Tests a dibenzylamino-substituted isoxazole as a structural alternative to the top pyrrolyl additive.
Probes the regioisomeric dibenzylamino isoxazole under the best observed catalyst-base pairing.
Tests a simple methylisoxazole to determine whether the top additive's pyrrolyl group is necessary.
Evaluates a compact dimethylisoxazole against the best observed catalyst-base pairing.
Tests the positional isomer of the simple methylisoxazole additive.
Assesses whether a phenyl substituent improves on the simple isoxazole additives.
Tests an electron-rich ester-substituted isoxazole for a distinct additive coordination and solubility profile.
Evaluates a methyl-substituted isoxazole ester as a contrasting polar additive.
Checks whether the dibenzylamino additive pairs effectively with the bulky BrettPhos-family ligand.
Tests a minimally substituted additive with AdBrettPhos and the best observed base.
Explores a different additive with BTMG to see whether it can rescue the weak initial L1 results.
Tests tBuXPhos with a simple additive and the most promising observed base.
